scope: Six codec-authored parser/held-reader/test files, existing file/lease primitives and actual CTest fixture binding; source-only review, no native/JVM build or subject execution in this review.
independence: Reviewer authored and froze the genuine Java oracle before inspecting this native implementation. This review is independent of codec native authorship; it does not independently requalify its own oracle providers or revise any Java expectations.

checks.evidence: Compared original complete Date/Date/RecordAccepter reader lines646–948 with the native branch flow. Baseline fields are parsed but ignored; s<=0 deactivates the positive anchor; valid delta/e before a positive anchor has no observation; anchored delta/e advances one reconstructed minute, e recorded time does not replace it and e does not clear it. Multiple starts reset, duplicate minutes add. Six field order matches LongTermStats constants.

Exact6/9 fields, VERSION1, ASCII signed decimal +/- and leading zeros, LF/CRLF/complete EOF, no bareCR,1MiB/8192nonblank/512-byte line bounds. Every record is validated including inactive/outside-day records. No malformed partial success. These are explicit differences from Java permissive skipping, ignored version/end-time parsing and unchecked arithmetic.

from_chars range classification is checked; add guards compute only representable max-positive/min-negative thresholds before addition. Local hourly/daily copies are committed only after all six checked sums; a failure discards the entire return value. s/e minute bounds are the truncating int64/60000 interval; reconstructed increment rejects MaximumMinute before stepping. Gregorian year1970..9999 keeps chrono day/minute products far inside int64. No borrowed input remains.

Empty/header-only/inactive files keep totals and all hours absent. An actual zero delta creates a present zero row and observation. Reconstructed selected-day interval is half-open and hour allocation is UTC; outside-day anchored records are validated/countable but not summed. Cancel returns no partial day.

Valid held lease and date are required. Exact stats/YYYY/MM/DD.dat only; no directory scan, cache.dat, recovery, writer, mkdir or second lease. Directory openat uses O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and compares named/opened identities. Selected regular leaf pre/post device/inode/size/mtime/ctime plus existing opened-file size/mtime checks detect observed changes. Missing component differs from present empty. Descriptor RAII preserves caller lease and owns only opened child fds.

Stop checks surround directory opening, bounded read, pure parse and publication; stop after an actual read wins over simultaneous read error. Invalid date/format/overflow/limits map InvalidFormat; unsupported version maps Unsupported; unsafe/raw IO is propagated; bad_alloc maps Io. No claim of syscall interruption or global allocation-free error construction.

21 named families include independent hand vectors for all six fields, positive gate, e reconstruction/retention, overlapping starts/hour boundaries/rollover, signed/plus/zero forms, presence vs unknown, ownership after input destruction, malformed/outside-day validation, int64 extrema and per-counter/cross-hour overflow, timestamp bounds and step limit, exact byte/line/record limits and prestop. Frozen oracle argv is mandatory, not optionally skipped.

11 named families expand generated private profiles: each missing path component/no creation; empty/header present; owned/copy/move result after lease release; exact padded date; no .bak/.saving/cache/neighbor use; moved lease and date rejection; directory/leaf symlink, regular/directory wrong shapes and FIFO fail safely. Test-private --wrap=read first invokes real read and matches exact owned dev/inode, then deterministically requests stop/IO or replaces/truncates leaf/month. Byte/inode/mode/nlink/mtime/ctime checks ignore atime appropriately. Cleanup is limited to explicitly created names.

All21 public files match the earlier frozen oracle receipt;17 data files match per-file manifest hashes. expected.tsv bytes equal preserved actual Java query.stdout. Its425 rows cover day plus24hours for each exact basename/date,2550 signed scalars. Consumer requires11 fields, bounded date/hour and leaf name, unique hourly slots and all25 slots per encountered fixture. CTest passes literal source fixtures/saved-history directory; linked core target uses actual saved_history.cpp. Reader target links profile with target-private --wrap=read. Both CTests remain120s.

fixture_binding.presence_mapping: Only scalar comparison maps native absent optional to Java returned zero. Native presence, observations, outside-day counts and strict errors receive zero Java equality credit.
fixture_binding.qualification_caveat: The consumer does not self-hash the corpus or hardcode17files/425rows. This review pins the full exact corpus; final qualification must retain that identity and report the actual2550 comparisons.

limits: Source PASS is not a compiler, sanitizer, native execution, UI or full-client parity result; root owns actual qualification.

Original Java Date reader clamps a future end time to now even when caches are disabled. Oracle dates are past the fixed2030 provider clock; native pure full-day projection has no clock and future/current-future-minute equality is not established.

Filesystem checks are separate observations, not a transaction against hostile swap-and-restore races or a promise that a held profile pathname can never be renamed. No extra uid/nlink rejection is invented for old regular history files.

Cancellation is cooperative at stated coarse boundaries; it does not interrupt blocking syscalls. Pure parser has no allocation; storage Error/string/read buffer allocation is not a global OOM guarantee.
No original writer/cache/global history service, persistent history writer, source UI graph/span behavior or original live profile was run by this review.
